beats.summary: Jim and Dwight discuss the search for an assistant to the assistant, with Dwight ultimately becoming the assistant to the assistant.

evidence.snippet: Jim: What I'm about to say makes no logical sense, and yet, it might be the most logical thing I've ever said.

beats.summary: Pam expresses concern to Jim about his happiness and their future after his return to Dunder Mifflin.

evidence.snippet: Pam: Because I'm so glad you're back, baby, but I'm just—I was talking to Darryl, and he was talking about the trip, and I just feel like you're giving up so much.

beats.summary: Darryl quietly leaves the warehouse without saying goodbye, upsetting his coworkers.

evidence.snippet: Darryl: No, no, I'm not here actually. These donuts are part of my escape from the guys at the warehouse I didn't say goodbye to.

beats.summary: Jim sets up an obstacle course coffee delivery challenge to test the abilities of potential assistants.

evidence.snippet: Jim: An assistant brings their boss coffee with speed and dexterity. But an assistant to the assistant has a thousand times more to prove, am I right?
Jim: Phyllis! Grab both these coffees, double-fist it, and head through this obstacle course.

beats.summary: Darryl resists spending sentimental time with coworkers after his departure but agrees to do one activity with them.

evidence.snippet: Darryl: Hey, hey, hey. I'll do one thing with y'all.
